rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy (Residential Tenant Protections)
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which is either an at-fault cause (such as nonpayment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, waste, criminal activity, or refusal of entry) or a no-fault cause taken in good faith (owner move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government order, or demolition or substantial remodel).
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies (lawful right to occupy for more than 30 days, excluding fixed-term leases of three months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego, including mobilehome park units, other than the exempt properties listed in §98.0703.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or agreement-restricted affordable housing; housing subject to affordable housing subsidy agreements (not including Section 8); mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care, licensed residential care, adult residential facilities and non-profit transitional housing; school and higher-education dormitories; units where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with a resident landlord; landlord-occupied single-family residences (including renting no more than two bedrooms, two ADUs or two JADUs, and mobilehomes); two-unit structures where the landlord occupies one unit as principal residence; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); and separately alienable property where the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management and tenants received the required written exemption notice.
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code §98.0704 (O-21647 N.S.; amended O-21769 N.S.)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.interaction_text: The rights conferred by this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or federal law.

rules.title: Owner move-in no-fault just cause conditions
rules.requirement: An owner move-in termination applies only if the intended occupant moves in within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the unit for at least 12 continuous months; otherwise the owner must offer the unit back to the former tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses beyond relocation assistance paid. For leases entered into on or after June 24, 2023, owner move-in applies only if the tenant agrees in writing or the lease expressly allows it.

rules.coverage_text: Owner move-in terminations of tenancies covered by the Residential Tenant Protections Division.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply if the intended occupant occupies a rental unit on the property or if a vacancy of a similar unit already exists at the property.
rules.penalty: If conditions are not met, the owner shall offer the unit to the vacated tenant at the same rent and lease terms and reimburse reasonable moving expenses in excess of relocation assistance paid.
rules.quoted_span: (E) Section 98.0704(b)(1) applies only if the intended occupant moves into the residential rental property within 90 days after the tenant vacates and occupies the residential rental property for at least 12 continuous months.

rules.title: Demolition or substantial remodel no-fault just cause requirements
rules.requirement: For terminations to demolish or substantially remodel, if permits are required the landlord must post the permit application at the property within three business days of submittal and secure the necessary permits before issuing the termination notice, which must include specified statements certified under penalty of perjury, including the tenant's right to re-rent if the work is not commenced or completed.
rules.coverage_text: Demolition or substantial remodel terminations of tenancies covered by the Residential Tenant Protections Division; substantial remodel requires the tenant to vacate for at least 30 continuous days.
